name: Defining relative clauses: who, which, that
subtitle: A relative clause tells you which person or thing you mean. Use who for people, which for things, and that for both: the woman who lives next door, the book which I bought, the film that we saw.
source: icanspeak English original English text (grammar-b1 run, 2026-10-29)

concept.exampleHtml: This is the woman who lives next door. — This is the book that I bought yesterday.

qa.html: who is for people. The man who fixed my bike is called Dan. I know a girl who speaks five languages. The relative clause comes straight after the noun it describes.

which is for things and animals. The phone which is on the table is mine. I like the cake which Zofia made. that works for people and things in defining clauses, and it is very common: the film that we saw, a girl that I know.

You can leave out who, which or that when it is the object of the clause. A noun or pronoun comes next: The book (that) I bought was cheap. The man (who) we met was kind. You must keep it when it is the subject. A verb comes next: The woman who lives next door is a doctor.
where is for places: The café where we met is closed. whose shows that something belongs to someone: The girl whose bike was stolen called the police.

Typical mistakes: ✗ The man which lives next door is a doctor. → ✓ The man who lives next door is a doctor. · ✗ The book what I read was long. → ✓ The book that I read was long. · ✗ The film that we saw it was good. → ✓ The film that we saw was good. (no extra it)

concept.noteHtml: This topic is about defining clauses: they tell you which person or thing. There is no comma. Extra information goes between commas, and then you can't use that: My sister, who lives in Leeds, is a nurse. A relative clause can end with a preposition: the man (that) I talked to. See Prepositions at the end. For whose and other ways to show who owns something, see 's or of. To say what someone does or did in the clause, you need the right tense: see Present simple and Past simple.

tables.caption: Examples
head: Word
Example
rows: The woman {who} lives next door is a doctor.
The bag {which} was on the train is mine.
The film {that} we saw was great.
The film we saw was great.
The café {where} we met is closed.
The girl {whose} bike was stolen called the police.

boxes.badge: Keep it or leave it out?
items: The man who called you is here. (A verb follows: keep who.)
The man (who) I called is here. (I follows: you can leave who out.)
The book (that) you lent me was good.
Rule: verb next → keep it. Noun or pronoun next → you can leave it out.
My sister, who lives in Leeds, is a nurse.
The commas show that this is extra information.
Here you can't use that, and you can't leave who out.

listen.text: The woman who lives next door is a doctor.
listen.note: who + verb: who is the subject, so you keep it.

listen.text: This is the book that I told you about.
listen.note: that is the object here. You can leave it out: the book I told you about.

listen.text: That's the café where we first met.

rounds.label: 1 · People: who
rounds.instruction: You hear two short sentences about a person. Join them with who.

example.prompt: I know a woman. She speaks five languages.
example.answer: I know a woman who speaks five languages.

items.prompt: Tom has a brother. He plays the drums.
items.answer: Tom has a brother who plays the drums.

items.prompt: I have a neighbour. She works at the hospital.
items.answer: I have a neighbour who works at the hospital.

items.prompt: This is the man. He fixed my bike.
items.answer: This is the man who fixed my bike.

items.prompt: Amira met a girl. She comes from Brazil.
items.answer: Amira met a girl who comes from Brazil.

items.prompt: Kwame has a friend. He teaches maths.
items.answer: Kwame has a friend who teaches maths.

items.prompt: We saw a doctor. She spoke Polish.
items.answer: We saw a doctor who spoke Polish.

rounds.label: 2 · Things: that
rounds.instruction: You hear two short sentences about a thing. Join them with that.

example.prompt: I lost the bag. I got it for my birthday.
example.answer: I lost the bag that I got for my birthday.

items.prompt: Here is the phone. I bought it last week.
items.answer: Here is the phone that I bought last week.

items.prompt: This is the film. We saw it on Friday.
items.answer: This is the film that we saw on Friday.

items.prompt: I like the cake. Zofia made it.
items.answer: I like the cake that Zofia made.

items.prompt: Where is the jacket? I wore it yesterday.
items.answer: Where is the jacket that I wore yesterday?

items.prompt: Liam found the keys. I lost them.
items.answer: Liam found the keys that I lost.

items.prompt: They live in a house. It has a red door.
items.answer: They live in a house that has a red door.

exercises.title: Who or which?
exercises.hint: Use who for people and which for things.

rows.term: the phone ... is on the table

exercises.title: who, which, whose or where?
exercises.hint: People: who. Things: which. Belongs to someone: whose. A place: where.
exercises.hintHtml: whofor peoplewhichfor thingswhosesomething belongs to someonewherefor places

items.prompt: The girl ___ bike was stolen called the police.
items.why: The bike belongs to the girl, so use whose.

items.prompt: That's the shop ___ I bought my shoes.
items.why: A shop is a place, so use where.

items.prompt: The woman ___ lives next door is a doctor.
items.why: The woman is a person, so use who.

items.prompt: The song ___ is playing now is my favourite.
items.why: A song is a thing, so use which.

items.prompt: I know a man ___ dog can sing.
items.why: The dog belongs to the man, so use whose.

items.prompt: This is the town ___ I grew up.
items.why: A town is a place, so use where.

items.prompt: Zofia is a friend ___ I met at university.
items.why: A friend is a person, so use who.

items.prompt: The bag ___ was on the train belongs to Mei.
items.why: A bag is a thing, so use which.

exercises.title: Can you leave it out?
exercises.hint: Look at the word after who, which or that. A verb follows: you must keep it. A noun or pronoun follows: you can leave it out.

items.prompt: The woman who lives next door is a doctor. Can you leave out who? ___
items.why: A verb (lives) follows. Who is the subject, so you must keep it.

items.prompt: The film that we saw was great. Can you leave out that? ___
items.why: A pronoun (we) follows. That is the object, so you can leave it out.

items.prompt: The man who phoned you is my uncle. Can you leave out who? ___
items.why: A verb (phoned) follows. Who is the subject.

items.prompt: The cake which Zofia made was lovely. Can you leave out which? ___
items.why: A noun (Zofia) follows. Which is the object.

items.prompt: The bus that goes to the airport is late. Can you leave out that? ___
items.why: A verb (goes) follows. That is the subject.

items.prompt: The shoes that she bought were expensive. Can you leave out that? ___
items.why: A pronoun (she) follows. That is the object.

items.prompt: The girl who sat next to me spoke Polish. Can you leave out who? ___
items.why: A verb (sat) follows. Who is the subject.

items.prompt: The jacket which I wore yesterday is dirty. Can you leave out which? ___
items.why: A pronoun (I) follows. Which is the object.

exercises.title: Two sentences → one sentence.
exercises.hint: Join the two sentences with who, which, that, whose or where. Don't repeat the person or thing.

rows.term: I met a man. He plays in a band.
rows.answer: I met a man who plays in a band.
choices: I met a man who plays in a band.
I met a man which plays in a band.
I met a man who he plays in a band.
I met a man what plays in a band.

rows.term: This is the film. I told you about it.
rows.answer: This is the film that I told you about.
choices: This is the film that I told you about.
This is the film that I told you about it.
This is the film who I told you about.
This is the film what I told you about.

rows.term: She has a cat. It is always hungry.
rows.answer: She has a cat which is always hungry.
choices: She has a cat which is always hungry.
She has a cat who is always hungry.
She has a cat which it is always hungry.
She has a cat whose is always hungry.

rows.term: Kwame has a friend. His mother is a pilot.
rows.answer: Kwame has a friend whose mother is a pilot.
choices: Kwame has a friend whose mother is a pilot.
Kwame has a friend who mother is a pilot.
Kwame has a friend which mother is a pilot.
Kwame has a friend whose his mother is a pilot.

rows.term: This is the café. We met here.
rows.answer: This is the café where we met.
choices: This is the café where we met.
This is the café which we met.
This is the café where we met there.
This is the café who we met.

exercises.title: What goes together?
exercises.hint: Tap the first part, then the part that finishes the sentence.

exercises.title: Gap text: A message to Diego.
exercises.hint: Choose who, which, that, where or whose. Think about the word before the gap: a person, a thing, a place or something that belongs to someone.

segments.text:
Hi Diego,

I'm so happy you're coming to Leeds! Here is some information about the flat. I live with a woman
works at the hospital. We have a kitchen
is very small, but we cook together every evening. There is a park near the flat
we often go running. I have a neighbour
dog barks all night, but he is very kind. The bus
goes to the centre stops outside. My friend

is visiting us next week is called Priya.

See you soon!
Mei
